The Delhi government will launch an enforcement drive from Octob- er 1 to make the system of Pollution Under Control (PUC) centres more eﬀective and reliable, Chief Minis- ter Rekha Gupta said on Saturday.  “We want to ensure that every person in Delhi gets clean air to breathe. This enforcement will be done to check whether the PUC certiﬁcates are valid,” she said. “The government’s objective is not merely to discuss the problem of pollution but to take concrete

long-term and eﬀective steps to control it,” Ms. Gupta added. Earlier in the day, Ms. Gupta in- augurated a ﬁve-lane automated testing station (ATS) in Burari with the capacity to conduct ﬁtness tests for one lakh vehicles annual- ly. Describing the ATS as “modern, transparent and technology-dri- ven”, Ms. Gupta said the initiative was part of the 360-degree eﬀorts to tackle pollution through better monitoring. ATS centres are now functional in Nand Nagri, Tehk- hand and Burari. Delhi’s automat- ed vehicle testing capacity exceeds 2.5 lakh vehicles annually.
Delhi to enforce PUC checks from Oct. 1, says CM Gupta

Four youths were killed and three injured after they were electrocuted when they were sleeping in a Ganpati pandal in Mad- hya Pradesh’s Mandla dis- trict, police said on Satur- day. According to police, the incident took place at 5 a.m. in Hirapur village when eight men were sleeping in the tent after re- turning from the immer- sion of Ganesh idol.

eavy rain disrupted normal life in Uttar Pradesh as the State bore the brunt of the depres- sion over north-east Madhya Pradesh and adjoining north Chhattisgarh. The weather system, which was moving to- wards south-east U.P., has brought heavy showers and as many as 63 districts recorded rainfall above normal, with some areas facing a moderate risk of ﬂash ﬂoods. Six persons were killed in separate  rain-related  inci- dents, with all the casualties reported  from  Lakhimpur Kheri, Amethi and Barabanki districts. The heavy rain, thunder- storms and strong winds also damaged standing crops in ru- ral areas and over 100 houses across the State as it received 19 times the normal rainfall in the past 24 hours, according to oﬃcials.

Lucknow recorded 125.8 mm of rainfall in the 21 hours ending Saturday morning; Far- rukhabad recorded 200 times its normal rainfall, while Kan- pur Nagar received 160 times and Kannauj, Kanpur Dehat and Hardoi 130 times the nor- mal rainfall. Uttar Pradesh Chief Minis- ter Yogi Adityanath on Satur- day directed oﬃcials to assess damage due to rainfall within 24 hours and provide all possi- ble assistance to aﬀected fami- lies.

Oﬃcials have been directed to take eﬀective measures ac- cording to local conditions for the safety of the public and to maintain special monitoring in sensitive areas.  Earlier, Relief Commission- er Hrishikesh Bhaskar Yashod held a video conference with the District Magistrates of dis- tricts under red and orange alerts and directed oﬃcials to ensure immediate action in the event of any emergency. Due to incessant rainfall in the catchment areas of the
Gandak river in Nepal, the bor- der districts and those vulner- able to the Gandak, Bagmati, and Kosi rivers have been in- structed to remain on high alert.

Review meeting Bihar Chief Secretary Pratyaya Amrit on Saturday chaired a high-level  review  meeting along with oﬃcials of the Dis- aster Management Depart- ment, Water Resources De- partment,  and  District Magistrates of 17 districts through videoconferencing. Districts put on high alert include  Sitamarhi,  West Champaran, East Champaran, Sheohar, Vaishali, Gopalganj, Saran, Madhubani, Darbhan- ga, Samastipur, Muzaﬀarpur, Saharsa, Supaul, Madhepura, Katihar,  Khagaria,  and Begusarai. Due to the rise in water le- vels of various rivers, nearly 50.49 lakh people have been aﬀected by ﬂoods across 578 gram panchayats in 15 districts in Bihar.

A day after winning the mayo- ral contests at the municipal corporations in Jaipur, Jodh- pur and Kota, the ruling Bhara- tiya Janata Party (BJP) on Satur- day registered victory for the deputy mayor’s posts in the three urban bodies. The BJP now has deputy mayors in all
the 10 municipal corporations in Rajasthan.

First woman dy. mayor BJP candidate Saroj Kanwar was elected as the ﬁrst woman deputy mayor in Jaipur after defeating Congress’s Salman Mansuri, a two-time Council- lor, with a margin of 31 votes. BJP’s Vijay Singh Panwar de- feated Congress candidate Ab-

dul Karim with a narrow mar- gin of four votes in Jodhpur. The BJP retained the deputy mayor’s post in the Kota Muni- cipal Corporation after party candidate Vivek Rajvanshi was elected unopposed.The Oppo- sition Congress boycotted the election and did not ﬁeld any candidate.  BJP’s Vikas Chauhan was elected deputy chairperson of

Suket municipality in Kota dis- trict. In Sikar district’s Kha- tushyamji municipality, where the counting of votes was done on Saturday on the order of the Rajasthan HC, Congress candidate Vinita Poonia was elected as the chairperson. In the counting of the 19 votes cast on September 21, Ms. Poo- nia secured 10 votes, while BJP’s Prem Devi received nine.
